newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-U.S. - MEXICO DRAW IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-U.S. - MEXICO DRAW IN WORLD CUP QUALIFIER.

text.p: The United States and Mexico drew 2-2 in a CONCACAF Region World Cup qualification game on Sunday.
The United States twice came from behind as it gained a vital point to move into second place in the group with five points from four games.
Mexico remains on top with eight points from four games. Costa Rica has four points from two games while Jamaica, Canada and El Salvador each have one point.

"That early goal took the wind out of our sails," U.S. coach Steve Sampson said, "but I think we played with poise and showed we had what it takes to come back. I'm very proud of what we accomplished."
Mexico opened the scoring in the first minute when U.S. goalkeeper Kasey Keller's failed clearance went off the face of Mexico forward Carlos Hermosillo into the empty net.
The U.S. overcame some sloppy passing and suspect defending late in the opening half with some probing runs from John Harkes, Ernie Stewart and Claudio Reyna.
The U.S. pulled level at 35 minutes through defender Eddie Pope.

Mexico defender Duilio Davino was cautioned for catching U.S. midfielder Reyna with a foot to the shoulder nearly 30 yards away from the Mexican goal. Reyna's ensuing restart was headed out of the Mexican area by Benjamin Galindo only to have Eric Wynalda head across to the left side where Pope slotted home from five yards out to the right post.
The game remained tied at the half.
"I'm happy to be back in Boston," Mexico coach Bora Milutinovic said. "This was an important result for both teams - I am happy to take a point and I am happy with my the enthusiasm of my players."
Milutinovic helped lead the U.S. to the second round of the 1994 World Cup. He was fired in 1995.
At 54 minutes, Galindo put Luis Hernandez through down the right side against the run of play. Hernandez made one touch and chipped Keller from 14 yards for the 2-1 advantage.

In the 69th minute, Hernandez was sent off for a hard tackle on Lalas, giving the U.S. a man advantage. Mexico's Galindo and Reyna will each miss their next game's through suspension after receiving second yellow cards.
The United States continued to press the attack and took advantage of an own goal from Mexican defender Nicolas Ramirez to pull level at 74 minutes.
A cross by Stewart was flicked on by Thomas Dooley to Ramirez who headed the ball back at goalkeerper Adolfo Rios. Ramirez' back pass went wide of Rios and into the goal along the left post.
The U.S. nearly found a game-winner when Harkes had a shot headed off the line by substitute Joaquin Del Almo at 89 minutes.

"We obviously wanted to take three points," said Keller, who helped Leicester City win the English League Cup on April 16. "It's tough. You think when you play at home, you should be taking maximum points."
At nine minutes, Mexico nearly took a 2-0 lead when Hernandez was sent through by Galindo on the right side only to have hit shot go wide to the right.
Mexico nearly went ahead before the interval when Alberto Garcia Aspe's shot from 30 yards carved inches wide of the left post at 43 minutes.
Teams:

United States -- 18-Kasey Keller; 3-Eddie Pope; 5-Thomas Dooley, (David Wagner, 77); 17-Marcelo Balboa; 22-Alexi Lalas (14-Michael Mason, 78); 12-Jeff Agoos; 6-John Harkes (capt); 16-Mike Sorber; 8-Ernie Stewart; 21-Claudio Reyna; 11-Eric Wynalda.

Mexico -- 25-Adolfo Rios; 2-Claudio Suarez; 5-Dullio Davino; 13-Pavl Pardo; 7-Ramon Ramirez (19-Richardo Pelaez, 90); 8-Alberto Garcia Aspe; 16-Alberto Coyote; 17-Benjamin Galindo (14-Joaquin Del Almo, 80); 27-Carlos Hermosillo; 15-Luis Hernandez; 11-Luis Roberto Alves (20-Nicolas Ramirz, 64).
Attendance: 54,407
Referee: Ubaldo Aquino Valenzano (Paraguay).
